A Turkish Airlines jet caught fire while landing at Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport in Nepal on Monday, with fire and smoke engulfing its right landing gear. Although the incident caused no reported injuries, it did force the airport to shut down.

According to the Associated Press and local media reports, the Turkish Airlines flight from Istanbul landed at Kathmandu's main airport with fire and smoke on the right landing gear. Emergency crew responded and controlled the fire, and passengers were safely evacuated, airport officials quoted by the media said.

More details: https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/turkish-airlines-jets-landing-gear-catches-fire-upon-arrival-at-nepals-kathmandu-tribhuvan-airport-video-101778470813096.html

India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi has issued a strong message amid the escalating West Asia oil crisis triggered by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking in Hyderabad during the launch of ₹9,400 crore development projects in Telangana, he urged citizens to use petrol, diesel and gas with great restraint. He also suggested work-from-home where possible and postponing foreign travel and large events to conserve fuel. As tensions linked to the US-Iran conflict continue to impact global oil supply, Modi highlighted India’s push toward solar energy, ethanol blending, LPG coverage and CNG expansion to reduce dependence on imports and strengthen security. The national capital is in for a wet and windy start to the week, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a “yellow alert” for Monday and Tuesday. A fresh western disturbance is likely to bring scattered showers and gusty winds of up to 50 km/hr across northwest India, including Delhi NCR.

Though the disturbance remains feeble, an IMD official said it began affecting the western Himalayan region from Sunday. “There are chances of light rain over the plains, including Delhi, on Monday and Tuesday,” the official added.
